checks: The normalized ratios of independent unit exponentials have the uniform simplex law, with the radial change of variables contributing the correct power d. Therefore the fixed family really has the displayed common ambient mass map.

For a proper chamber at least two phases are nonzero. The added-phase characteristic products decay sufficiently for both density and first density-derivative inversion, uniformly on compact coefficient neighborhoods in the chamber.

Differentiate the mollified step under expectation with exponential moment domination. Exponential size bias adds one phase to the first derivative, two independent phases to a mixed derivative, and two phases with coefficient two on the diagonal. Integration by parts gives the negative sign on the density derivative.
For either sign of c, the distributional resolvent (1+c d/dx) k_c=delta_0 has the stated sign from the boundary jump at zero. Subtracting the two resolvents gives P_ij=(P_i-P_j)/(c_i-c_j).

An independent triangular check uses P(1,2,-3)=1-9/(4*5) in the two-positive chamber. The derivatives are P_1=9/80, P_2=9/100, P_3=39/400 and P_13=3/800, agreeing with the cross-sign divided difference. Degree-zero homogeneity gives Hc=-grad P and the ordinary linear chain rule gives the joint ambient derivatives.

The original f2be43e7a9dbeca5 §1 uses one common normal and no independent fiberwise variations. Its common orientation case is a specialization of the frozen formula, and the enlarged signed regularity is supplied directly by the proof.

overlap.comparison: This proves the single-simplex joint C² law and centroid identity with at least two positive and one negative phase, including zero margins. The frozen result instead covers all strict proper sign chambers, including one positive phase, and gives cross-sign divided differences and the finite-family pullback.
This supplies positive-pair Hessian formulas on its stated sign range. It does not cover the full strict signed divided difference or the common ambient pullback.
